vocabulary.example: What does your sister look like?

grammar.explanation_en: When using several adjectives, English follows an order: opinion, size, age, then other qualities — 'a nice, tall, young man'. Use 'look like + noun' to describe appearance ('She looks like a model') but 'look + adjective' for a direct description ('She looks tired').
grammar.explanation_ko: 여러 형용사를 쓸 때 영어는 순서가 있습니다: 의견, 크기, 나이, 기타 특징 순 — 'a nice, tall, young man'. 외모를 묘사할 때 'look like + 명사'('She looks like a model')와 'look + 형용사'('She looks tired')를 구별해서 씁니다.

examples.en: He is a tall, young man.
She looks like her older sister.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: What does your new coworker look like?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: She's tall, with short curly hair. She's also very friendly.
dialogue.line_ko: 키가 크고 짧은 곱슬머리예요. 아주 다정하기도 해요.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: I think she's in her late twenties.

reading.title: My Best Friend
reading.text: My best friend, Mina, is in her twenties. She is tall and has long, straight hair. She wears glasses and looks very smart. Mina has a wonderful personality — she is kind, funny, and always ready to help others. People say she looks like her father.
reading.text_ko: 제 가장 친한 친구 미나는 20대예요. 키가 크고 길고 곧은 머리를 가지고 있어요. 안경을 쓰고 아주 똑똑해 보여요. 미나는 성격이 훌륭해요 — 친절하고 재밌고 항상 남을 도울 준비가 되어 있어요. 사람들은 그녀가 아버지를 닮았다고 해요.

explanation.en: The text says 'has long, straight hair.'
The text says 'she looks like her father.'
